student.dashboard.title: Dashboard
student.dashboard.summary: Your academic home. It shows your current standing, how your GPA is moving, and the most useful next step.

terms.term: CGPA, PI, Degree class, At risk
terms.meaning: See the glossary.
The GPA (or PI) of your latest semester.

tasks.title: Switch the headline between CGPA and PI
steps: Open Settings.
Change Primary metric.

tasks.title: See every course
steps: Open Results (Android: View All).

tasks.title: Act on the suggestion
steps: Follow the next-step card, for example "Complete pending scores".

cautions: The degree class is a projection from your graded courses, not your university's official result.

web: The "AI insight" card shows your last saved Written Analysis summary.
android: When offline, the app shows your saved data and syncs your changes later.
Carry-overs appear here when you have any, with their units.
Set a degree goal here or in What-If to see the GPA your remaining semesters need, the highest CGPA you can still reach, and what keeps your current class.

student.results.title: Results
student.results.summary: Lists every semester in your programme timeline, with its GPA, credits and courses.

terms.meaning: A semester that is not complete yet. Its graded courses already count toward CGPA; it joins Insights and the transcript when you complete it.
Included in Insights and the transcript.

tasks.title: Add the next semester
steps: Choose Add semester (Android: Create next semester).

tasks.title: Edit a semester
steps: Open it.

tasks.title: Delete a semester
steps: Choose Delete.
Confirm. Its courses go with it and your CGPA is recalculated.

cautions: Deleting cannot be undone.
If all programme semesters already exist, increase your programme duration in Settings to add another year.

student.new-semester.title: New semester
student.new-semester.summary: Creates the next missing semester from your entry session and programme duration, so levels and sessions are never duplicated or skipped.

tasks.title: Create the next semester
steps: Check the level, semester and session shown.
Choose Create.
You land in the new semester.

cautions: Only the next valid semester can be created.
If you see "Academic timeline needed", set your entry session (YYYY/YYYY) and programme duration in Settings first.

student.semester.title: Semester
student.semester.summary: Holds one semester's courses. Here you enter scores, scan a result slip, swap course lists with classmates, and complete the semester.

terms.meaning: CA 0–30 and exam 0–70; the total and grade are calculated for you.
1–6 per course.
Awaiting result (left out of GPA).
The course still needs a score or grade.

tasks.title: Add a course
steps: Enter the code, title and units.
Enter CA and exam, or a letter grade.
Save.

tasks.title: Scan a result slip
steps: Choose Scan (web: Import Result Slip).
Review what was found.
Confirm.

tasks.title: Share your course list
steps: Choose Share.
Send the 6-character code.

tasks.title: Use a classmate's code
steps: Choose Import.
Enter the code.
Fill in your own scores.

tasks.title: Finish the semester
steps: Complete it (web: Save Semester; Android: Complete semester).

cautions: A course code shares course names and units only, never scores.
You need at least 3 courses to create a code.
Completing needs at least one graded course; on Android every imported course needs a score or grade first.

web: Importing a code replaces the course list you are editing. (Planned: merge, as on Android.)
android: Importing skips courses already in the semester.

student.course-entry.title: Add or edit a course
student.course-entry.summary: Records one course and shows the grade and points it will give before you save.

tasks.title: Enter by score
steps: Type CA (0–30) and exam (0–70).

tasks.title: Enter by grade
steps: Switch to Letter Grade.
Pick A–F.

tasks.title: Result not out yet
steps: Switch to Awaiting result.
Type your CA (optional) to see the exam score out of 70 that each grade needs.

cautions: With a letter grade only, PI uses that grade's points, so it is an estimate.
An awaiting-result course stays out of GPA until you enter the exam score. The exam guidance is an estimate; your institution decides your final grade.
Nothing is added until you save.

android: Typing a course code suggests courses from the course catalogue. Choosing one fills the code, title and units, never scores.

student.course-codes.title: Course codes
student.course-codes.summary: Copies a semester's course list (codes, titles, units) between classmates with a 6-character code.

tasks.title: Share
steps: Choose Share.
Copy the code.

tasks.title: Import
steps: Enter a classmate's code.
Import.
Add your own scores.

cautions: Codes contain no scores, grades or personal details.
Anyone with the code can import the list.
Codes do not expire.

student.scanner.title: Result scanner
student.scanner.summary: Reads course codes, units and scores from a photo, image or PDF of your result, then lets you check everything before it is saved.

terms.meaning: Scanning has its own daily free uses, and is also limited to 5 scans per 15 minutes.

tasks.title: Scan
steps: Lay the slip flat in even light.
Keep all columns in the frame.
Capture (or choose an image or PDF).
Review.
Confirm.

tasks.title: If something is wrong
steps: Edit it in review, or choose Enter details manually.

cautions: Nothing is saved until you confirm.
Unreadable scores are left as "Add score" rather than guessed.
Courses marked AR on the slip are saved as awaiting result.

android: When free scans run out and coins are on, you can pay with coins; failed scans refund them.

student.insights.title: Insights
student.insights.summary: Four tools for planning. Forecast projects your trend. What-If works out the GPA you need. Risk Analysis lists carry-overs and low grades. Written Analysis gives AI advice.

tasks.title: Get help for a tool
steps: Pick a tab.
Open Help again for that tab.

cautions: Insights use every graded course. Courses awaiting a result are left out.
When your programme timeline is complete, projections stop at graduation.

student.insights.forecast.title: Forecast
student.insights.forecast.summary: Projects your CGPA or PI for your next semesters from your completed results.

tasks.title: Switch views
steps: Switch between the CGPA and PI views.

tasks.title: Update after new results
steps: Choose Refresh forecast after adding results.

cautions: A forecast is reused for up to 1 hour if your results have not changed. That reuse does not use a free use.
New forecasts are limited to 2 per hour and to your daily free uses.

android: Shows up to the next 2 semesters in your timeline.

student.insights.whatif.title: What-If
student.insights.whatif.summary: Works out the GPA you would need in your remaining semesters to reach a target CGPA. You can ask AI whether that is realistic.

terms.meaning: (target × (credits so far + future credits) − current CGPA × credits so far) ÷ future credits. Above 5.00 means the target cannot be reached in that time.
The average percentage that would give that number as a PI, i.e. required GPA ÷ 5 × 100. Grades use bands, so a lower score can still earn the grade points (any score from 70 earns an A).

tasks.title: Test a target
steps: Move the target.
Set the remaining semesters and units per semester.
Read the result.
Optionally choose Get AI guidance.

cautions: The maths is instant and free.
AI guidance is limited to 3 requests per 5 minutes and to your daily free uses.

android: Remaining semesters are capped by your timeline, and units default to 18. Guidance has a 30-second wait between requests.
Your saved degree goal sits above the calculator. If a goal can no longer be reached, it says so and suggests the best class still possible.

student.insights.risk.title: Risk Analysis
student.insights.risk.summary: Lists carry-overs (failed courses you have not yet passed in a later semester) separately from low grades (D, E or F), with an overall risk level from your saved results and forecast. Courses awaiting a result are left out.
cautions: Opening this tab never makes an AI request.
Your department's rules decide which failed courses you must retake, for example when an elective is replaced.

student.insights.analysis.title: Written Analysis
student.insights.analysis.summary: AI-written strengths, concerns, recommendations and degree outlook based on your completed results.

terms.meaning: Your last analysis stays readable at any time.
Makes a new analysis; free regeneration is allowed once every 12 hours, within your daily free uses.

tasks.title: Update after new results
steps: Add your results.
Choose Regenerate when the "Your results changed" note appears.

cautions: If the AI is unavailable you will see your last saved analysis.
Advice is guidance, not an official academic decision.

android: Coins on: when free uses run out you can pay coins.
Coins off: you may watch a rewarded ad for one extra refresh (max 2 a day). The extra refresh is only granted after the ad network confirms the reward to our server, which can take a moment.

student.transcript.title: Transcript
student.transcript.summary: Builds an unofficial transcript from your completed semesters. A summary at the top shows your CGPA, class, units and grading scale. Below it you can save a PDF, share a link, see your shared links and preview a transcript someone sent you.

terms.meaning: Generated by AcadeGrade, not by your university.
A public link to a snapshot of your record.

tasks.title: Save or send a PDF
steps: Choose Download PDF on the website, or Share PDF in the Android app.
Turn Include my photo on or off first if you want to change it.
On the website you can also choose Print.

tasks.title: Share a link
steps: Choose Share a link.
Pick how long it works: 1, 7 or 30 days.
Pick Full transcript or Summary only, and turn Include my photo on or off.
Add a PIN if you want one (optional), then create the link.
Copy the link or show its QR code.

tasks.title: Manage shared links
steps: Each link has a card under Shared links showing when it expires, what it shows, whether it has a PIN or photo, and how many views it has.
Use Copy, QR or Open on a card.
To stop a link working, choose Delete and confirm.

tasks.title: Preview a transcript
steps: Under Preview a transcript, paste a share link or the code at the end of it.
Enter the PIN if asked.
The transcript opens exactly as the person with the link sees it.

cautions: Anyone with the link can view it until it expires or you delete it.
The link shows your record at the moment you created it; create a new one after adding results.
Opening a link, including in Preview a transcript, counts as a view.
Transcript CGPA covers completed semesters only.

student.notifications.title: Notifications
student.notifications.summary: Your inbox for semester saves, degree-class changes, new AI insights and announcements from AcadeGrade.

tasks.title: Read
steps: Tap an item.

tasks.title: Mark all read
steps: Choose Mark all read.

tasks.title: Choose which alerts you get
steps: Open Settings.
Go to Notifications.

web: Clear all deletes every notification in your inbox.

terms.meaning: A message from AcadeGrade to all students or to your university or level. It stays until it ends; marking it read only applies on this device.

cautions: Clear all hides announcements on this device; it does not delete them for anyone else.

student.settings.title: Settings
student.settings.summary: Your profile, academic timeline, display preferences, notifications and account security.

terms.meaning: The year you started (YYYY/YYYY, consecutive years).
Years in your programme (1–10). Together these define which semesters you can create.
Whether your dashboard leads with CGPA or PI.

tasks.title: Fix your timeline
steps: Change the entry session or duration.
Save.

tasks.title: Turn alerts on or off
steps: Switch Semester saved, Degree class change, AI insights ready, or Admin broadcasts.

tasks.title: Delete your account
steps: Choose Delete account.
Confirm with your password (web: also type DELETE).

cautions: Deleting your account erases all semesters, courses, transcript links and your profile, and cannot be undone.
Matric number changes need the AcadeGrade team.

web: Also has Profile picture, Change password, Push notifications for this browser, and Record mode. Record mode is saved but does not change calculations.
android: Also has Appearance, App Lock, App updates, Share AcadeGrade, Export transcript, and Replay usage guide.

Download my data shares a JSON file of your profile, results, saved insights and notifications, or a CSV of your courses. The files contain your grades, so on a shared phone delete any copy left behind.
Screen privacy: Discreet mode hides your CGPA, GPA and grades until you tap them. Block screenshots and hide app preview also blocks your own screenshots. Both apply to this phone only and start off.

student.glossary.title: Terms used in AcadeGrade
student.glossary.summary: What each number and label in AcadeGrade means, exactly as the apps calculate it.

terms.meaning: A 70–100 = 5 · B 60–69 = 4 · C 50–59 = 3 · D 45–49 = 2 · E 40–44 = 1 · F 0–39 = 0. This scale is built into both apps.
Your semester's grade points weighted by credit units: Σ(grade point × units) ÷ Σ(units). Only courses with a score or grade count.
Your cumulative GPA: every graded course, weighted by its credit units, whether or not its semester is marked complete. Courses awaiting a result (AR) or still needing a score are left out.

Like GPA, but it uses your exact score instead of the grade band: each course gives (total ÷ 100) × 5 points, weighted by units. For example, 69% gives PI points of 3.45 but grade points of 4 (a B). If you entered a letter grade only, PI uses that grade's points (an estimate).

Based on CGPA. First Class 4.50–5.00 · Second Class Upper (2:1) 3.50–4.49 · Second Class Lower (2:2) 2.40–3.49 · Third Class 1.50–2.39 · Pass 1.00–1.49 · Fail below 1.00. It is a projection, not your university's official award.
1–6 per course. More units mean the course moves your GPA more.

A course whose result is not out yet (your slip may mark it "AR"). It shows "AR" and is left out of GPA, PI and credits until the exam score is entered. You can still save its CA to see the exam score each grade needs.
A course saved without scores (for example, imported from a course code, or a scan with an unreadable score). Android will not complete the semester until each one has a score or grade.

A semester you marked complete (web: saved with at least one graded course; Android: "Complete semester"). Completed semesters count toward Insights and the transcript; CGPA also includes graded courses in semesters still in progress.
A graded course with a D, E or F. A carry-over is an F you have not yet passed in a later semester.
A failed (F) course you have not passed in a later semester. Its units are shown as outstanding. Courses awaiting a result never count. Your department's rules decide what you must retake.

Each AI feature has its own free allowance per 24-hour window. The window starts at your first request for that feature and is not a midnight reset. There is also a short-term limit (Written Analysis and Forecast 2 per hour; What-If 3 per 5 minutes; scanning 5 per 15 minutes).

A saved answer shown again without a new AI request, so it does not use a free use. Forecasts are reused for up to 1 hour when your results have not changed. Written Analysis stays readable until you regenerate it, and free regeneration is allowed once every 12 hours.

Points you earn by watching a short rewarded ad on Android, and spend when a feature's free uses run out. They are not money and cannot be bought or transferred. There are daily earning limits, a maximum balance, and a daily limit of coin uses per feature. If a coin-paid request fails, the coins are refunded. Earning and spending days reset at midnight UTC.
When coins are off, a verified rewarded ad on Android gives one extra Written Analysis refresh, up to 2 per day (UTC).
A 6-character code that copies a semester's course list (code, title, units) to a classmate. It never includes scores or grades. You need at least 3 courses to create one. Codes do not expire.

A public web link to a snapshot of your completed semesters. It expires after 30 days, and you can delete it sooner. It shows the record as it was when you created it; make a new link after adding results.
Whether your dashboard leads with CGPA or PI. It changes the display only, not the calculations.
Your course scores averaged by credit units, over courses with a score. Grade-only and awaiting-result courses are left out. Not a CGPA, not official, and not a 4.0-scale grade.

student.semester-preview.title: Preview expected grades
student.semester-preview.summary: For courses still awaiting a result, guess a grade to see how your GPA, CGPA and class could change. Guesses stay on this device and are never saved to your record.

terms.meaning: Your figures from saved results only.
The same figures if your expected grades come true.

tasks.title: Try an expected grade
steps: Open a semester with an awaiting-result course.
Pick a grade under Preview expected grades.
Compare Official with your guesses.

tasks.title: Clear a guess
steps: Set the course back to Not sure.

cautions: A preview is not a result and never changes your CGPA.
Guesses are removed when you sign out.

student.credit-load.title: Usual units per semester
student.credit-load.summary: Set the fewest and most units you normally take. A semester outside that range, or a course entered twice, shows a gentle note. It never stops you saving.

tasks.title: Set your range
steps: Open Settings, then your academic settings (web: Academic Setup).
Enter the fewest and most units (1 to 60).
Choose Save range.

tasks.title: Remove your range
steps: Empty both boxes.
Save again.

cautions: Awaiting-result courses count toward the units you registered.
Without a range, only repeated course codes are flagged.

student.milestones.title: Milestones
student.milestones.summary: AcadeGrade marks positive moments: your first completed semester, a personal-best semester GPA, a move up a class, clearing every carry-over and completing your programme.

tasks.title: Dismiss a milestone
steps: Choose the close button on the New milestone card.

cautions: Each milestone is celebrated once.
Awaiting-result courses never count toward a milestone.
Milestones you had already reached before this feature are recorded quietly.

student.semester-recap.title: Semester recap
student.semester-recap.summary: After you complete a semester, a short recap shows its GPA and change, units earned, your strongest course, any class change and carry-overs you cleared.

tasks.title: Close the recap
steps: Choose Done. It will not open again for that semester.

tasks.title: Get a Written Analysis
steps: Choose Get a Written Analysis in the recap.
It opens Insights on the Written Analysis tab.

cautions: The Written Analysis link only appears when AI features are available to you.

student.support.title: Help and support
student.support.summary: Send a problem or question to the AcadeGrade team and read our replies.

terms.meaning: We have your request and will reply.
We replied. The reply is also in your Notifications and your email.
Done. Closed requests are deleted 180 days later.

tasks.title: Report a problem
steps: Open Settings, then Help and support.
Choose what it is about.
Describe the problem in at least 10 characters.
Choose Send request.

tasks.title: Read a reply
steps: Open Notifications, or Your requests under Help and support.

cautions: Never include your password or any code we sent you.
You can send 3 requests an hour and 10 a day.
Text only: screenshots cannot be attached.

student.timetable.title: Timetable
student.timetable.summary: Keeps your lectures, classes, exams and study sessions in one place. Each timetable is valid for a number of hours, days, weeks or months, and you can extend it.

terms.meaning: A timetable you type in yourself, such as your lectures and exams.
A study timetable, made by hand or with Build with AcadeMind.
Any other timetable you want to keep.
How long the timetable runs. Weekly events stop when it ends.
The timetable ends within the next hour, day, 3 days or 7 days, depending on its length.

tasks.title: Make a timetable
steps: Open Timetable.
Choose New timetable.
Pick Fixed, Reading or Custom, then how long it is valid for.
Add your events.

tasks.title: Build a reading plan
steps: Choose Build with AcadeMind.
Add subjects, days, study times and how long the plan runs.
Review the preview, then save it.

tasks.title: Extend a timetable
steps: Choose Extend on the ending soon or expired notice.
It runs again for the same length, counted from today.

cautions: Build with AcadeMind follows fixed rules shown in its preview; you can change the plan before saving.
Archived and expired timetables do not send reminders.

android: Reminders come as notifications, even offline. They may arrive a few minutes late on some phones.
Some phones stop background reminders: allow AcadeGrade in Settings > Apps > AcadeGrade > Battery > Unrestricted.
web: The website does not send reminders. Download the .ics file and your calendar app will remind you.

student.share-link-controls.title: Transcript link controls
student.share-link-controls.summary: Choose how long a transcript link lasts, whether it shows courses or just a summary, whether it shows your photo, and whether it needs a PIN.

tasks.title: Choose how long a link lasts
steps: Open Transcript and choose Share a link.
Pick 1, 7 or 30 days.

tasks.title: Share a summary only
steps: In Share a link, pick Summary only instead of Full transcript.
The link shows semester totals and your CGPA, not course scores.

tasks.title: Protect a link with a PIN
steps: In Share a link, enter a 4 to 6 digit PIN.
Send the PIN separately from the link.

cautions: We cannot show or recover a PIN. If you forget it, delete the link and make a new one.
After 10 wrong tries a link locks for an hour.
A 6 digit PIN is harder to guess than a 4 digit one.

student.share-code-link.title: Course code links
student.share-code-link.summary: Share a course list code as a link. Classmates see course codes, titles and units only, never your scores.

tasks.title: Share a code
steps: Open a semester.
Create or export a code.
Copy or share the link and send it to a classmate.

tasks.title: Open a shared link
steps: Open the link.
Sign in if asked.
Check the code, then choose Import courses.

cautions: If you have several semesters in progress, you choose where to import.
Nothing is saved until you save the semester.

student.paste-portal.title: Paste from portal
student.paste-portal.summary: Copy your course rows from your university portal and paste them in to fill a semester faster.

tasks.title: Import results
steps: Copy the course rows from your portal.
Open a semester and choose the paste option.
Review the courses it finds.
Fill in any missing scores, then save.

cautions: Nothing is saved until you confirm.
Lines that cannot be read are skipped and counted; add them by hand.
Pasted text is read on your device and is not sent for AI analysis, so it works for everyone.

student.coin-history.title: Coin history
student.coin-history.summary: Your last coin changes: earned, spent, refunded or given, with the balance after each.

tasks.title: See your coin history
steps: Open a feature that shows credits.
Choose Coin history or Coin activity.

cautions: Coins are not money and cannot be bought or transferred.
Accounts that cannot use AI features have no coin history.

student.entry-level.title: Direct entry and spill-over
student.entry-level.summary: If you started in 200L or 300L, set your entry level so your timeline starts there. Spill-over semesters come after your final level.

tasks.title: Set it at sign-up
steps: Choose your entry level: 100L, or 200L or 300L for direct entry.
Add spill-over semesters only if you already know you will stay longer.

cautions: Course duration counts from 100L, so direct entry has fewer years.

student.privacy-devices.title: Devices and sign-out
student.privacy-devices.summary: See which devices get notifications from your account, remove one, or sign out everywhere.

tasks.title: Remove a device
steps: Open Settings, then Security and data.
Find the device under Devices.
Choose Remove.

tasks.title: Sign out everywhere
steps: Open Settings, then Security and data.
Choose Sign out everywhere.
Confirm.

cautions: Other devices are signed out within an hour, not instantly.
A device is listed only after it turns notifications on.
Change your password too if you think someone else has access.

student.data-saver.title: Data saver
student.data-saver.summary: Uses less data by turning off animations and optional background loading.

tasks.title: Turn Data saver on
steps: Open Settings.
Switch Data saver on.

cautions: Your results still save and sync as usual.
It applies to this browser or phone only.

student.olevel.title: WAEC and NECO results
student.olevel.summary: Add up to two sittings. We take your best grade in each subject; A1–C6 are credits. Most courses need five credits including English and Maths.

tasks.title: Add a sitting
steps: Open your O-level results.
Choose Add a sitting, then pick the exam and the year.
Add each subject and its grade. A sitting holds up to nine subjects.

tasks.title: Waiting for a result
steps: Pick Awaiting (AR) as the grade.
It does not count as a credit until you change it.

cautions: D7 and E8 are passes, not credits. F9 is a fail.
Check the exact subjects with your school. Some courses also need a particular subject, such as Physics or Biology.
Nothing here is sent to WAEC, NECO or JAMB. It is your own record.

web: Under Subjects your course needs, add the subjects your course asks for. We show which ones you have a credit in and which are missing.

student.admission.title: Admission aggregate
student.admission.summary: Pick your school's formula. Your aggregate is an estimate out of 100; check your school's published formula.

tasks.title: Work out your aggregate
steps: Enter your UTME score, out of 400.
Enter your post-UTME score and what it is out of. Leave the score empty until you have it.
Pick the formula your school uses.

tasks.title: Use your O-level grades
steps: If your formula counts O-level, use the grades from your WAEC or NECO results, or type five grades.
English and Maths always count. The best three other subjects make up the five.

tasks.title: Set a target
steps: Enter the aggregate you are aiming for, out of 100.
We show the post-UTME score you need to reach it.
Save, and your target is kept with your scores.

cautions: This is an estimate. Schools change their formulas, so check your school's published formula.
If your school uses its own weights, pick My school's weights and enter them.

student.record-type.title: Record type
student.record-type.summary: Switch between university, WAEC/NECO and JAMB tracking. Nothing is deleted when you switch.

tasks.title: Switch what you track
steps: Open Settings, then Record type.
Pick university, WAEC or NECO, or JAMB and admission.
Confirm the switch.

cautions: Your other records are kept. Switch back and they are all still there.
To switch to university tracking you may need to add your school details first.
AcadeMind and the other AI features are only for university tracking.
